chapter: Instruments, tenors and the current band
title: Gregory Herbert, a virtuoso who stayed himself
summary: Herman praises Gregory Herbert as a phenomenal saxophonist and flutist who carried tradition while remaining himself.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Speaking about that, you had an endless string of very, very fine tenor players.
Right.
Probably as many as anybody in the entire history of --
Well, whatever, I was proud of most of those guys, believe me, because they were expressing their own thoughts, to a great degree.
Could we just run through a few of those because I think that one instrument is such an --
Yeah. The first person that comes in my head because of the closeness of the years and everything is -- I would like to start with Gregory Herbert.
Oh, good.

Who I think is a virtuoso, and I've always thought so. He had all the attributes of every oldtime saxophone player, but he never relied on it, never worked on it. He still was Gregory Herbert. And this is a thing I really demand in great players.
I know that when he -- with the soloing on something that came from a particular period, that you could see that he was carrying on the tradition but he was still Greg.
He was completely Greg.
Yeah. Then he moved to something else that was contemporary, he was still Greg.
Right. He had a giant scope. And I didn't -- once again, I get carried away, but I really feel
badly when I see -- it's all the potential, blow it up the drainpipe.
Can we talk a little bit more about Gregory, because he was such a --
Phenomenal saxophonist, phenomenal flutist. He was one of the giants of this period of music in my band.
Uh-huh.
To be able to play a ballad and play it on all kinds of peoples' programs and --
And what I understand, too, from Frank Tiberi, that he was an eager learner, always open to --
That's right.
-- hear more things, find out about more things.
Of course, he was a very bright and together young man.
Yeah.
I had the utmost respect and admiration for him. He was one of the prettiest players I've ever heard in my life, who could still turn around and so the wildest, funkiest thing and (inaudible), right?
Right, right.
Including the children of today.
Yeah, you just turn him around. An incredible player.
Right. He had an asset that wouldn't quit.
